# Game Hosting Guides

> Independent reviews and comparisons of Minecraft and game server hosting providers. We test hosts in real-world conditions and publish results as long-form written reviews and YouTube videos.

## Reviews

- [Best Minecraft Server Hosting 2026 — comparison](https://gamehostingguides.com/best-minecraft-server-hosting/): Side-by-side comparison of 9 providers with disclosed hardware specs, pricing, and datacenter locations.
- [Apex Hosting review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/apex-hosting/): Polished, well-supported Minecraft host with 18 datacenter locations and one-click modpacks.
- [BisectHosting review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/bisecthosting/): 2,300+ modpack library and 21 global datacenters; Budget vs Premium tier comparison.
- [CloudNord review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/cloudnord/): EU-native hosting with publicly disclosed Ryzen 7 7700 / i9-11900K hardware.
- [Hostinger review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/hostinger/): VPS-based Minecraft hosting with AMD EPYC and KVM virtualization.
- [MCProHosting review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/mcprohosting/): Legacy creator-partnered host, now operating under Apex Hosting after Nitrado acquisition.
- [Nodecraft review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/nodecraft/): Polished NodePanel with one-click swap between 59+ games on the same server.
- [Server.pro review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/server-pro/): Genuinely free tier with a real paid upgrade path.
- [ServerPrism review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/serverprism/): Single plan splittable across multiple game servers, proxies, databases, and bots.
- [Shockbyte review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/shockbyte/): Budget Minecraft hosting with global node coverage including Sydney and Singapore.
